subject: Transition at the IRONMAN World Championship, Kailua-Kona
editorial: KONA.m independent room. Facts below are sourced; race-craft notes are general, not the rules of any specific race.

facts.line: The swim starts in Kailua Bay: the pro men at 6:20 am and the pro women at 6:30 am (2026).
The bike leaves directly from the Kailua Pier transition area, and the run starts from the same transition point.
The finish line is on Aliʻi Drive.

race_craft.line: T1 is the change from swim to bike; T2 is the change from bike to run. The clock keeps running through both.
Most races mark a line you must cross on foot before you get on the bike, and another where you get off.
Long-distance races often hand each athlete gear bags for the bike and the run instead of a box beside the bike.
Transitions are practised like any other discipline: the same order every time, nothing new on race day.
